children.text: Chapter 1
kaścit kāntāvirahaguruṇā svādhikārāt pramattaḥ śāpenāstaṃgamitamahimā varṣabhogyeṇa bhartuḥ
children.translated_text: A certain <s>yakṣa</s>, made heedless of his own duty by the heavy sorrow of separation from his beloved, had his greatness brought to an end by his master's curse, to be endured for a year.

children.text: yakṣaścakre janakatanayāsnānapuṇyodakeṣu snigdhachāyātaruṣu vasatiṃ rāmagiryāśrameṣu ||
children.translated_text: He made his dwelling in the hermitages of <s>Rāmagiri</s>, among trees with tender shade and waters made holy by the bathing of <s>Janaka</s>'s daughter.

children.text: tasminnadrau katicidabalāviprayuktaḥ sa kāmī nītvā māsānkanakavalayabhraṃśariktaprakoṣṭhaḥ
children.translated_text: On that mountain, separated from his helpless beloved, that longing one passed some months, his forearm left bare by the slipping of its golden bracelet.

children.text: āṣāḍhasya prathamadivase meghamāśliṣṭasānuṃ vaprakrīḍāpariṇatagajaprekṣaṇīyaṃ dadarśa ||
children.translated_text: On the first day of <s>Āṣāḍha</s> he saw a cloud embracing the peak, lovely to behold like an elephant bent down in play against a bank.

children.text: tasya sthitvā kathamapi puraḥ kautukādhānahetorantarbāṣpaściram anucaro rājarājasya dadhyau
children.translated_text: Standing somehow before it, because it had stirred his wonder, the attendant of the king of kings pondered for a long time, with tears held within.

children.text: meghāloke bhavati sukhino 'pyanyathāvṛtti cetaḥ kaṇṭhāśleṣapraṇayini jane kiṃ punardūrasaṃsthe ||
children.translated_text: At the sight of a cloud even the mind of a happy man takes another turn; how much more so when the loved one who yearns for an embrace of the neck is far away.

children.text: pratyāsanne nabhasi dayitājīvitālambanārthī jīmūtena svakuśalamayīṃ hārayiṣyan pravṛttim
children.translated_text: When the rainy season was near, wishing to sustain the life of his beloved, and intending to send by the cloud news of his own welfare,

children.text: sa pratyagraiḥ kuṭajakusumaiḥ kalpitārghāya tasmai prītaḥ prītipramukhavacanaṃ svāgataṃ vyājahāra ||
children.translated_text: he, pleased, offered that cloud an argha fashioned from fresh <s>kuṭaja</s> blossoms and spoke words of welcome, with affection foremost.

children.text: dhūmajyotiḥsalilamarutāṃ saṃnipātaḥ kva meghaḥ saṃdeśārthāḥ kva paṭukaraṇaiḥ prāṇibhiḥ prāpaṇīyāḥ
children.translated_text: What is a cloud, a conjunction of smoke, light, water, and wind? And what are messages, fit to be conveyed by living beings with capable senses?

children.text: ityautsukyādaparigaṇayan guhyakastaṃ yayāce kāmārtā hi prakṛtikṛpaṇāścetanācetaneṣu ||
children.translated_text: So thinking, yet from eagerness disregarding the difference, the <s>guhyaka</s> begged it; for those afflicted by love are by nature pitiable toward sentient and insentient things alike.

children.text: jātaṃ vaṃśe bhuvanavidite puṣkarāvartakānāṃ jānāmi tvāṃ prakṛtipuruṣaṃ kāmarūpaṃ maghonaḥ
children.translated_text: I know you, born in the world-renowned lineage of the <s>Puṣkara</s> and <s>Āvartaka</s> clouds, a primal being of <s>Maghavan</s>, able to assume forms at will.

children.text: tenārthitvaṃ tvayi vidhivaśāddūrabandhurgato 'haṃ yācñā moghā varam adhiguṇe nādhame labdhakāmā ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, because fate has made me a petitioner and my kinsman is far away, I have come to you. A request made to one of excellence is better, even if fruitless, than one fulfilled by an inferior.

children.text: saṃtaptānāṃ tvamasi śaraṇaṃ tatpayoda priyāyāḥ saṃdeśaṃ me hara dhanapatikrodhaviśleṣitasya
children.translated_text: You are the refuge of the tormented; therefore, O rain-cloud, carry my message to my beloved, from me who have been separated by the anger of the lord of wealth.

children.text: gantavyā te vasatir alakā nāma yakṣeśvarāṇāṃ bāhyodyānasthitaharaśiraścandrikādhautaharmyā ||
children.translated_text: Your destination is the dwelling called <s>Alakā</s>, of the lords of the <s>yakṣas</s>, its mansions washed by the moonlight from <s>Hara</s>'s head as he stands in the outer garden.

children.text: tvām ārūḍhaṃ pavanapadavīm udgṛhītālakāntāḥ prekṣiṣyante pathikavanitāḥ pratyayādāśvasantyaḥ
children.translated_text: Women whose husbands are on journeys, their curls lifted up, will look at you as you mount the path of the wind, taking heart from the confidence that you bring rain.

children.text: kaḥ saṃnaddhe virahavidhurāṃ tvayyupekṣeta jāyāṃ na syādanyo 'pyahamiva jano yaḥ parādhīnavṛttiḥ ||
children.translated_text: When you are ready, who would neglect a wife distressed by separation? There can be no other person like me, whose course depends on another's will.

children.text: tvāṃ cāvaśyaṃ divasagaṇanātatparām ekapatnīmavyāpannāmavihatagatirdrakṣyasi bhrātṛjāyām
children.translated_text: And you, moving unobstructed, will surely see my single wife, intent on counting the days, unharmed: your brother's wife, as it were.

children.text: āśābandhaḥ kusumasadṛśaṃ prāyaśo hyaṅganānāṃ sadyaḥ pāti praṇayi hṛdayaṃ viprayoge ruṇaddhi ||
children.translated_text: For the bond of hope usually holds back the flower-like heart of women in separation, O lover; otherwise it would fall at once.

children.text: mandaṃ mandaṃ nudati pavanaścānukūlo yathā tvāṃ vāmaścāyaṃ nadati madhuraṃ cātakaste sagandhaḥ
children.translated_text: As a favorable wind gently, gently urges you on, and this fragrant <s>cātaka</s> on your left cries sweetly,

children.text: garbhādhānakṣaṇaparicayān nūnam ābaddhamālāḥ seviṣyante nayanasubhagaṃ khe bhavantaṃ balākāḥ ||
children.translated_text: surely the cranes, having formed lines because they know the moment for conception, will attend upon you in the sky, beautiful to the eye.

children.text: kartuṃ yacca prabhavati mahīm ucchilīndhrām avandhyāṃ tacchrutvā te śravaṇasubhagaṃ garjitaṃ mānasotkāḥ
children.translated_text: And when they hear your thunder, pleasing to the ear, which has power to make the earth fertile and covered with sprouting mushrooms, the royal geese, longing for <s>Mānasa</s>,

children.text: ā kailāsādbisakisalayacchedapātheyavantaḥ sampatsyante nabhasi bhavato rājahaṃsāḥ sahāyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: with bits of lotus-fiber shoots as provisions from <s>Kailāsa</s> onward, will become your companions in the sky.

children.text: āpṛcchasva priyasakham amuṃ tuṅgam āliṅgya śailaṃ vandyaiḥ puṃsāṃ raghupatipadairaṅkitaṃ mekhalāsu
children.translated_text: Take leave of this dear friend, the lofty mountain, embracing it, marked on its slopes by the venerable footprints of the lord of the <s>Raghus</s>.

children.text: kāle kāle bhavati bhavato yasya saṃyogametya snehavyaktiściravirahajaṃ muñcato bāṣpamuṣṇam ||
children.translated_text: Whenever it comes into contact with you at the proper times, it shows its affection born from long separation by releasing hot tears.

children.text: mārgaṃ tāvacchṛṇu kathayatas tvatprayāṇānurūpaṃ saṃdeśaṃ me tadanu jalada śroṣyasi śrotrapeyam
children.translated_text: First listen as I describe the route suited to your journey; afterward, O cloud, you will hear my message, fit to be drunk in by the ear.

children.text: khinnaḥ khinnaḥ śikhariṣu padaṃ nyasya gantāsi yatra kṣīṇaḥ kṣīṇaḥ parilaghu payaḥ srotasāṃ copabhujya ||
children.translated_text: Where, weary again and again, you will travel by setting your foot on mountain peaks, and, diminished again and again, you will partake of the light waters of streams.

children.text: adreḥ śṛṅgaṃ harati pavanaḥ kiṃsvid ityunmukhībhir dṛṣṭotsāhaś cakitacakitaṃ mugdhasiddhāṅganābhiḥ
children.translated_text: With innocent <s>siddha</s> women looking upward in startled fear, thinking, 'Can the wind be carrying off the mountain peak?', while they have seen your boldness,

children.text: sthānād asmāt sarasaniculād utpatodaṅmukhaḥ khaṃ diṅnāgānāṃ pathi pariharan sthūlahastāvalepān ||
children.translated_text: rise from this place rich with moist <s>nicula</s> reeds, facing north into the sky, avoiding on the path the heavy trunk-strokes of the elephants of the quarters.

children.text: ratnacchāyāvyatikara iva prekṣyametatpurastād valmīkāgrāt prabhavati dhanuḥkhaṇḍam ākhaṇḍalasya
children.translated_text: Ahead of you, this fragment of <s>Ākhaṇḍala</s>'s bow, a rainbow, appears from the top of an anthill, as if it were a mingling of jewel-colors.

children.text: yena śyāmaṃ vapur atitarāṃ kāntim āpatsyate te barheṇeva sphuritarucinā gopaveṣasya viṣṇoḥ ||
children.translated_text: By it your dark body will gain surpassing beauty, like <s>Viṣṇu</s> dressed as a cowherd, with a peacock feather of flashing radiance.

children.text: tvayyāyattaṃ kṛṣiphalam iti bhrūvikārān abhijñaiḥ prītisnigdhairjanapadavadhūlocanaiḥ pīyamānaḥ
children.translated_text: Since the fruit of farming depends on you, you will be drunk in by the loving, moist eyes of village women, skilled in expressive movements of the eyebrows.

children.text: sadyaḥ sīrotkaṣaṇasurabhi kṣetram āruhya mālaṃ kiṃcit paścād vraja laghugatir bhūya evottareṇa ||
children.translated_text: Mount the <s>Māla</s> field, at once fragrant from the fresh turning of the furrow, then go somewhat westward, and afterward north again with swift motion.

children.text: tvām āsārapraśamitavanopaplavaṃ sādhu mūrdhnā vakṣyaty adhvaśramaparigataṃ sānumān āmrakūṭaḥ
children.translated_text: The mountain <s>Āmrakūṭa</s>, whose forest fires you have quenched with showers, will rightly bear you on its head when you are overcome by the fatigue of the road.

children.text: na kṣudro 'pi prathamasukṛtāpekṣayā saṃśrayāya prāpte mitre bhavati vimukhaḥ kiṃ punar yas tathoccaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even a lowly one, when a friend has come for shelter, does not turn away, remembering a former kindness; how much less one who is so lofty.

children.text: channopāntaḥ pariṇataphaladyotibhiḥ kānanāmrais tvayy ārūḍhe śikharam acalaḥ snigdhaveṇīsavarṇe
children.translated_text: When you have mounted its peak, whose margins are hidden by forest mango trees bright with ripened fruit, and you are the color of glossy braided hair,

children.text: nūnaṃ yāsyaty amaramithunaprekṣaṇīyām avasthāṃ madhye śyāmaḥ stana iva bhuvaḥ śeṣavistārapāṇḍuḥ ||
children.translated_text: the mountain, dark in the middle and pale in its remaining expanses, will surely attain a state lovely for immortal couples to behold, like a breast of the earth.

children.text: sthitvā tasmin vanacaravadhūbhuktakuñje muhūrtaṃ toyotsargadrutataragatis tatparaṃ vartma tīrṇaḥ
children.translated_text: After staying there for a moment in bowers enjoyed by forest-dwelling women, then, your speed made swifter by the release of water, you will have crossed the next stretch of road.

children.text: revāṃ drakṣyasyupalaviṣame vindhyapāde viśīrṇāṃ bhakticchedair iva viracitāṃ bhūtim aṅge gajasya ||
children.translated_text: You will see the <s>Revā</s>, broken upon the uneven stones at the foot of the <s>Vindhya</s>, as though the sacred ash on an elephant's body had been arranged in broken stripes.

children.text: adhvaklāntaṃ pratimukhagataṃ sānumānāmrakūṭas tuṅgena tvāṃ jalada śirasā vakṣyati ślāghamānaḥ
children.translated_text: When you, weary from the road, come before it, the mountain <s>Āmrakūṭa</s>, full of respect, will proudly receive you, O cloud, with its lofty summit.

children.text: āsāreṇa tvam api śamayes tasya naidāgham agniṃ sadbhāvārdraḥ phalati na cireṇopakāro mahatsu ||
children.translated_text: And you too should quench its summer fire with a downpour; a service, when moistened by good feeling, bears fruit before long among the noble.

children.text: tasyās tiktair vanagajamadair vāsitaṃ vāntavṛṣṭir jambūkuñjapratihatarayaṃ toyam ādāya gaccheḥ
children.translated_text: After pouring out rain, take up water from that river, scented with the pungent ichor of forest elephants and slowed by groves of rose-apple trees, and go on.

children.text: antaḥsāraṃ ghana tulayituṃ nānilaḥ śakṣyati tvāṃ riktaḥ sarvo bhavati hi laghuḥ pūrṇatā gauravāya ||
children.translated_text: O dense cloud, the wind will not be able to weigh you when you are full within; everything empty is light, while fullness gives weight.

children.text: nīpaṃ dṛṣṭvā haritakapiśaṃ kesarair ardharūḍhair āvirbhūtaprathamamukulāḥ kandalīś cānukaccham
children.translated_text: Seeing the <s>nīpa</s> trees greenish-brown with half-grown filaments, and the plantain shoots along the marshy banks with their first buds appearing,

children.text: jagdhvāraṇyeṣv adhikasurabhiṃ gandham āghrāya corvyāḥ sāraṅgās te jalalavamucaḥ sūcayiṣyanti mārgam ||
children.translated_text: and smelling the earth's fragrance made especially sweet in the forests where elephants have eaten, the deer will show you the way, O releaser of drops of water.

children.text: ambhobindugrahaṇacaturāṃś cātakān vīkṣamāṇāḥ śreṇībhūtāḥ parigaṇanayā nirdiśanto balākāḥ
children.translated_text: Watching the <s>cātaka</s> birds skilled at catching drops of water, and the cranes arranged in rows as though pointing out the count,

children.text: tvām āsādya stanitasamaye mānayiṣyanti siddhāḥ sotkampāni priyasahacarīsambhramāliṅgitāni ||
children.translated_text: the <s>siddhas</s>, when they meet you at the time of thunder, will honor you with trembling embraces from their beloved companions, given in alarm.

children.text: utpaśyāmi drutamapi sakhe matpriyārthaṃ yiyāsoḥ kālakṣepaṃ kakubhasurabhau parvate parvate te
children.translated_text: Friend, although you are eager to go quickly for the sake of my beloved, I foresee delays for you on mountain after mountain fragrant with <s>kakubha</s> flowers.

children.text: śuklāpāṅgaiḥ sajalanayanaiḥ svāgatīkṛtya kekāḥ pratudyātaḥ katham api bhavān gantum āśu vyavasyet ||
children.translated_text: Welcoming you with cries, their pale eye-corners and water-filled eyes, the peacocks will urge you on; somehow you must resolve to go swiftly.

children.text: pāṇḍucchāyopavanavṛtayaḥ ketakaiḥ sūcibhinnair nīḍārambhair gṛhabalibhujām ākulagrāmacaityāḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>Daśārṇa</s> country will become lined with pale-shaded gardens pierced by needle-like <s>ketaka</s> blossoms, its village shrines crowded by house-crows beginning their nests,

children.text: tvayy āsanne pariṇataphalaśyāmajambūvanāntāḥ sampatsyante katipayadinasthāyihaṃsā daśārṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, when you are near, its outskirts of rose-apple woods dark with ripened fruit will have swans staying only for a few days.

children.text: teṣāṃ dikṣu prathitavidiśālakṣaṇāṃ rājadhānīṃ gatvā sadyaḥ phalam avikalaṃ kāmukatvasya labdhā
children.translated_text: After going to their capital, widely known in all directions by the mark of <s>Vidiśā</s>, you will at once obtain the complete fruit of being a lover,

children.text: tīropāntastanitasubhagaṃ pāsyasi svādu yasmāt sabhrūbhaṅgaṃ mukham iva payo vetravatyāś calormi ||
children.translated_text: for there you will drink the sweet water of the <s>Vetravatī</s>, lovely with thunder near its banks, like a face with moving waves and a frown of eyebrows.

children.text: nīcairākhyaṃ girim adhivases tatra viśrāmahetos tvatsamparkāt pulakitam iva prauḍhapuṣpaiḥ kadambaiḥ
children.translated_text: There, for rest, you should dwell upon the mountain called <s>Nīcaiḥ</s>, which, from contact with you, seems thrilled with fully blossomed <s>kadamba</s> trees.

children.text: yaḥ puṇyastrīratiparimalodgāribhir nāgarāṇām uddāmāni prathayati śilāveśmabhir yauvanāni ||
children.translated_text: With its rock-houses exhaling the perfumes of the love-play of courtesans, it displays the unrestrained youthfulness of the townsmen.

children.text: viśrāntaḥ san vraja vananadītīrajānāṃ niṣiñcannudyānānāṃ navajalakaṇair yūthikājālakāni
children.translated_text: When rested, go on, sprinkling with fresh drops of water the lattices of <s>yūthikā</s> jasmine in the gardens born on the banks of forest rivers,

children.text: gaṇḍasvedāpanayanarujāklāntakarṇotpalānāṃ chāyādānāt kṣaṇaparicitaḥ puṣpalāvīmukhānām ||
children.translated_text: and, by giving shade, become for a moment familiar with the faces of the flower-picking women, whose ear-lotuses are tired from the painful wiping away of sweat from their cheeks.

children.text: vakraḥ panthā yadapi bhavataḥ prasthitasyottarāśāṃ saudhotsaṅgapraṇayavimukho mā sma bhūr ujjayinyāḥ
children.translated_text: Although the road is indirect for you as you set out toward the northern quarter, do not turn away from intimacy with the palace terraces of <s>Ujjayinī</s>.

children.text: vidyuddāmasphuritacakitais tatra paurāṅganānāṃ lolāpāṅgair yadi na ramase locanair vañcito 'si ||
children.translated_text: If there you do not delight in the restless sidelong eyes of the city women, startled by the flashing of your chains of lightning, you are cheated of eyes.

children.text: vīcikṣobhastanitavihagaśreṇikāñcīguṇāyāḥ saṃsarpantyāḥ skhalitasubhagaṃ darśitāvartanābhaḥ
children.translated_text: On the road, meet the <s>Nirvindhyā</s>, whose rows of birds are a girdle-string made noisy by the agitation of waves, who moves along with graceful stumbling and shows her navel in her eddies;

children.text: nirvindhyāyāḥ pathi bhava rasābhyantaraḥ saṃnipatya strīṇām ādyaṃ praṇayavacanaṃ vibhramo hi priyeṣu ||
children.translated_text: enter deeply into her waters, for among women the first speech of love toward beloveds is playful coquetry.

children.text: veṇībhūtapratanusalilā tām atītasya sindhuḥ pāṇḍucchāyā taṭaruhatarubhraṃśibhirjīrṇaparṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: After you pass her, there is the river reduced to a thin braid of water, pale with old leaves fallen from trees growing on her banks.

children.text: saubhāgyaṃ te subhaga virahāvasthayā vyañjayantī kārśyaṃ yena tyajati vidhinā sa tvayaivopapādyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: O fortunate one, she reveals by her condition of separation your good fortune; the very means by which she may abandon her emaciation must be supplied by you alone.

children.text: prāpyāvantīn udayanakathākovidagrāmavṛddhān pūrvoddiṣṭām upasara purīṃ śrīviśālāṃ viśālām
children.translated_text: After reaching <s>Avanti</s>, where the village elders are skilled in the tales of <s>Udayana</s>, approach the great and splendid city, <s>Viśālā</s>, mentioned earlier.

children.text: svalpībhūte sucaritaphale svargiṇāṃ gāṃ gatānāṃ śeṣaiḥ puṇyair hṛtam iva divaḥ kāntimat khaṇḍam ekam ||
children.translated_text: It is as though a single radiant fragment of heaven had been brought down by the remaining merits of heaven-dwellers whose fruit of good deeds had become small and who had come to earth.

children.text: dīrghīkurvan paṭu madakalaṃ kūjitaṃ sārasānāṃ pratyūṣeṣu sphuṭitakamalāmodamaitrīkaṣāyaḥ
children.translated_text: There, in the early mornings, the wind of the <s>Śiprā</s>, lengthening the sharp, intoxicated cries of cranes and astringent with friendship for the fragrance of opened lotuses,

children.text: yatra strīṇāṃ harati surataglānim aṅgānukūlaḥ śiprāvātaḥ priyatama iva prārthanācāṭukāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: takes away the love-weariness from women's bodies, agreeable to their limbs like a lover skilled in flattering petitions.

children.text: hārāṃs tārāṃs taralaguṭikān koṭiśaḥ śaṅkhaśuktīḥ śaṣpaśyāmān marakatamaṇīn unmayūkhaprarohān
children.translated_text: Seeing in that city necklaces, bright pearls, trembling beads, conches and shells by the tens of millions, grass-green emeralds shooting forth rays,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā yasyāṃ vipaṇiracitān vidrumāṇāṃ ca bhaṅgān saṃlakṣyante salilanidhayas toyamātrāvaśeṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and pieces of coral arranged for sale in the market, one understands that the oceans have only water left.

children.text: pradyotasya priyaduhitaraṃ vatsarājo 'tra jahre haimaṃ tāladrumavanam abhūd atra tasyaiva rājñaḥ
children.translated_text: Here <s>Vatsarāja</s> carried off the beloved daughter of <s>Pradyota</s>; here there was a golden grove of palmyra trees belonging to that same king.

children.text: atrodbhrāntaḥ kila nalagiriḥ stambham utpāṭya darpād ity āgantūn ramayati jano yatra bandhūn abhijñaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here, they say, <s>Nalagiri</s>, maddened with pride, wandered after uprooting a post: in such a place the knowing townsman delights visiting kinsmen with these tales.

children.text: jālodgīrṇair upacitavapuḥ keśasaṃskāradhūpair bandhuprītyā bhavanaśikhibhir dattanṛtyopahāraḥ
children.translated_text: With your body increased by hair-dressing incense issuing through lattices, and with the household peacocks, out of affection for a kinsman, offering you the gift of dance,

children.text: harmyeṣv asyāḥ kusumasurabhiṣv adhvakhedaṃ nayethā lakṣmīṃ paśyaṃl lalitavanitāpādarāgāṅkiteṣu ||
children.translated_text: you should remove the fatigue of the road on her flower-fragrant mansions, seeing their splendor marked by the red lac from the feet of graceful women.

children.text: bhartuḥ kaṇṭhacchavir iti gaṇaiḥ sādaraṃ vīkṣyamāṇaḥ puṇyaṃ yāyās tribhuvanaguror dhāma caṇḍīśvarasya
children.translated_text: Regarded respectfully by the attendants as the hue of their master's neck, you should go to the holy abode of <s>Caṇḍīśvara</s>, the teacher of the three worlds.

children.text: dhūtodyānaṃ kuvalayarajogandhibhir gandhavatyās toyakrīḍāniratayuvatisnānatiktair marudbhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: It has gardens shaken by breezes from the <s>Gandhavatī</s>, fragrant with the pollen of blue lotuses and made pungent by the bathing of young women intent on water-play.

children.text: apyanyasmiñjaladhara mahākālam āsādya kāle sthātavyaṃ te nayanaviṣayaṃ yāvad atyeti bhānuḥ
children.translated_text: And, cloud, when at another time you have reached <s>Mahākāla</s>, you must remain until the sun has passed beyond the range of sight.

children.text: kurvan saṃdhyābalipaṭahatāṃ śūlinaḥ ślāghanīyām āmandrāṇāṃ phalam avikalaṃ lapsyase garjitānām ||
children.translated_text: Making for <s>Śūlin</s> a praiseworthy drumbeat for the evening offering, you will obtain the full reward of your deep thunderings.

children.text: pādanyāsaiḥ kvaṇitaraśanās tatra līlāvadhūtai ratnacchāyākhacitavalibhiś cāmaraiḥ klāntahastāḥ
children.translated_text: There, with anklets ringing from their steps and hands tired by playfully waved cāmaras whose folds are inlaid with jewel-light,

children.text: veśyās tvatto nakhapadasukhān prāpya varṣāgrabindūn āmokṣyante tvayi madhukaraśreṇidīrghān kaṭākṣān ||
children.translated_text: the courtesans, receiving from you the pleasure of first raindrops on their nail-marks, will cast toward you sidelong glances long as rows of bees.

children.text: paścād uccairbhujataruvanaṃ maṇḍalenābhilīnaḥ sāṃdhyaṃ tejaḥ pratinavajapāpuṣparaktaṃ dadhānaḥ
children.translated_text: Afterwards, merged in a circle within the high forest of uplifted arms, bearing evening radiance red like freshly opened hibiscus flowers,

children.text: nṛttārambhe hara paśupater ārdranāgājinecchāṃ śāntodvegastimitanayanaṃ dṛṣṭabhaktir bhavānyā ||
children.translated_text: at the beginning of the dance, remove <s>Paśupati</s>'s desire for a moist elephant-hide; <s>Bhavānī</s>, her agitation stilled and eyes motionless, will see your devotion.

children.text: gacchantīnāṃ ramaṇavasatiṃ yoṣitāṃ tatra naktaṃ ruddhāloke narapatipathe sūcibhedyais tamobhiḥ
children.translated_text: At night, when women there go to their lovers' dwellings and the royal road is blocked from sight by darkness dense enough to be pierced by a needle,

children.text: saudāmanyā kanakanikaṣasnigdhayā darśayorvīṃ toyotsargastanitamukharo mā ca bhūr viklavāstāḥ ||
children.translated_text: show the ground with lightning smooth as gold on a touchstone; do not become noisy with rain-discharge and thunder, lest they be frightened.

children.text: tāṃ kasyāṃcid bhavanavalabhau suptapārāvatāyāṃ nītvā rātriṃ ciravilasanāt khinnavidyutkalatraḥ
children.translated_text: Having spent the night on the roof-terrace of some house where the pigeons are sleeping, your lightning-wife weary from long flashing,

children.text: dṛṣṭe sūrye punarapi bhavān vāhayedadhvaśeṣaṃ mandāyante na khalu suhṛdām abhyupetārthakṛtyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: when the sun is seen, you should again make the remainder of the road; those who have undertaken a friend's business do not, indeed, grow slack.

children.text: tasmin kāle nayanasalilaṃ yoṣitāṃ khaṇḍitānāṃ śāntiṃ neyaṃ praṇayibhir ato vartma bhānos tyajāśu
children.translated_text: At that time the tears of offended women must be brought to rest by their lovers; therefore quickly leave the path of the sun.

children.text: prāleyāstraṃ kamalavadanāt so 'pi hartuṃ nalinyāḥ pratyāvṛttastvayi kararudhi syād analpābhyasūyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For he too, turned back when you obstruct his rays, would have no little jealousy, since he means to take the frost-drop tears from the lotus-faced <s>Nalinī</s>.

children.text: gambhīrāyāḥ payasi saritaś cetasīva prasanne chāyātmāpi prakṛtisubhago lapsyate te praveśam
children.translated_text: In the clear water of the river <s>Gambhīrā</s>, as in a clear mind, even your shadow-form, lovely by nature, will gain entrance.

children.text: tasmād asyāḥ kumudaviśadāny arhasi tvaṃ na dhairyān moghīkartuṃ caṭulaśaphorodvartanaprekṣitāni ||
children.translated_text: Therefore you should not, out of firmness, make fruitless her glances, bright as white water-lilies and restless with the turning of darting śaphara fish.

children.text: tasyāḥ kiṃcit karadhṛtam iva prāptavānīraśākhaṃ hṛtvā nīlaṃ salilavasanaṃ muktarodhonitambam
children.translated_text: Taking away her blue garment of water, as it were, from the reed-branch that seems held in her hand, while her bank-hips are laid bare,

children.text: prasthānaṃ te kathamapi sakhe lambamānasya bhāvi jñātāsvādo vivṛtajaghanāṃ ko vihātuṃ samarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: your departure, friend, will somehow come only with delay; who, once he has known the taste, is able to leave a woman with her loins uncovered?

children.text: tvanniṣyandocchvasitavasudhāgandhasamparkaramyaḥ srotorandhradhvanitasubhagaṃ dantibhiḥ pīyamānaḥ
children.translated_text: Pleasant from contact with the fragrance of the earth breathing out through your outpouring, and beautiful with the sound made through the openings of its streams, drunk by elephants,

children.text: nīcair vāsyaty upajigamiṣor devapūrvaṃ giriṃ te śīto vāyuḥ pariṇamayitā kānanodumbarāṇām ||
children.translated_text: a cool wind, ripener of forest figs, will blow gently upon you as you desire to approach the mountain once called <s>Deva</s>.

children.text: tatra skandaṃ niyatavasatiṃ puṣpameghīkṛtātmā puṣpāsāraiḥ snapayatu bhavān vyomagaṅgājalārdraiḥ
children.translated_text: There, having made yourself into a cloud of flowers, let yourself bathe <s>Skanda</s>, who has his fixed abode there, with showers of flowers moist with the water of the heavenly <s>Gaṅgā</s>.

children.text: rakṣāhetor navaśaśibhṛtā vāsavīnāṃ camūnām atyādityaṃ hutavahamukhe saṃbhṛtaṃ taddhi tejaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For that fire-like brilliance, surpassing the sun, was gathered in the mouth of Fire by the bearer of the new moon for the protection of <s>Indra</s>'s armies.

children.text: jyotirlekhāvalayi galitaṃ yasya barhaṃ bhavānī putrapremṇā kuvalayadalaprāpi karṇe karoti
children.translated_text: The peacock-feather of his, dropped with a surrounding streak of light, <s>Bhavānī</s>, from love for her son, places at her ear, reaching to a petal of blue lotus.

children.text: dhautāpāṅgaṃ haraśaśirucā pāvakes taṃ mayūraṃ paścād adrigrahaṇagurubhir garjitair nartayethāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then make that peacock, whose eye-corners are washed by the moonlight of <s>Hara</s>, dance with thunderclaps heavy enough to seize a mountain.

children.text: ārādhyainaṃ śaravaṇabhavaṃ devam ullaṅghitādhvā siddhadvandvair jalakaṇabhayād vīṇibhir muktamārgaḥ
children.translated_text: Having worshipped this god born in the reed-bed, and having crossed the road, while pairs of Siddhas who carry vīṇās leave the path for fear of water-drops,

children.text: vyālambethāḥ surabhitanayālambhajāṃ mānayiṣyan srotomūrtyā bhuvi pariṇatāṃ rantidevasya kīrtim ||
children.translated_text: you should hang down, intending to honor <s>Rantideva</s>'s fame, born from the slaughter of the daughter of <s>Surabhi</s> and transformed on earth into the form of a stream.

children.text: tvayy ādātuṃ jalam avanate śārṅgiṇo varṇacaure tasyāḥ sindhoḥ pṛthum api tanuṃ dūrabhāvāt pravāham
children.translated_text: When you bend down to take water from that river, thief of the color of <s>Śārṅgin</s>, the sky-goers will surely look upon her current, broad in body yet thin because of distance,

children.text: prekṣiṣyante gaganagatayo nūnam āvarjya dṛṣṭir ekaṃ muktāguṇam iva bhuvaḥ sthūlamadhyendranīlam ||
children.translated_text: turning their gaze, as if it were a single string of pearls of the earth, with a large sapphire at its middle.

children.text: tām uttīrya vraja paricitabhrūlatāvibhramāṇāṃ pakṣmotkṣepād uparivilasatkṛṣṇaśāraprabhāṇām
children.translated_text: Crossing her, go on, making your own reflection the object of the eager eyes of the women of <s>Daśapura</s>, whose familiar creeper-like eyebrows are playful, whose dark gazelle-like radiance flashes above with the lifting of their eyelashes,

children.text: kundakṣepānugamadhukaraśrīmuṣām ātmabimbaṃ pātrīkurvan daśapuravadhūnetrakautūhalānām ||
children.translated_text: and whose beauty steals that of bees following the tossing of jasmine blossoms.

children.text: brahmāvartaṃ janapadam atha chāyayā gāhamānaḥ kṣetraṃ kṣatrapradhanapiśunaṃ kauravaṃ tad bhajethāḥ
children.translated_text: Then, entering with your shade the country of <s>Brahmāvarta</s>, you should visit that <s>Kaurava</s> field, which bears witness to the destruction of warriors.

children.text: rājanyānāṃ śitaśaraśatair yatra gāṇḍīvadhanvā dhārāpātais tvam iva kamalāny abhyavarṣan mukhāni ||
children.translated_text: There <s>Gāṇḍīvadhanvan</s> rained hundreds of sharp arrows upon the faces of kings, as you rain streams of water upon lotuses.

children.text: hitvā hālām abhimatarasāṃ revatīlocanāṅkāṃ bandhuprītyā samaravimukho lāṅgalī yāḥ siṣeve
children.translated_text: Those waters of the <s>Sarasvatī</s> were served by <s>Lāṅgalin</s>, who, for love of his kinsmen, turned away from battle, after leaving liquor dear in taste and marked by <s>Revatī</s>'s eyes.

children.text: kṛtvā tāsām adhigamam apāṃ saumya sārasvatīnām antaḥ śuddhas tvam api bhavitā varṇamātreṇa kṛṣṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having obtained those waters, gentle one, you too will become inwardly pure, though black in color only.

children.text: tasmād gaccher anu kanakhalaṃ śailarājāvatīrṇāṃ jahnoḥ kanyāṃ sagaratanayasvargasopānapaṅktim
children.translated_text: From there you should go on toward <s>Kanakhala</s>, to the daughter of <s>Jahnu</s>, descended from the king of mountains, a stairway-row to heaven for the sons of <s>Sagara</s>.

children.text: gaurīvaktrabhrukuṭiracanāṃ yā vihasyeva phenaiḥ śambhoḥ keśagrahaṇam akarod indulagnormihastā ||
children.translated_text: As if laughing with her foam at <s>Gaurī</s>'s frowning face, she grasped <s>Śambhu</s>'s hair with wave-hands to which the moon was attached.

children.text: tasyāḥ pātuṃ suragaja iva vyomni paścārdhalambī tvaṃ ced acchasphaṭikaviśadaṃ tarkayes tiryag ambhaḥ
children.translated_text: If, like the elephant of the gods, you should lean your rear half down in the sky to drink her water, clear and bright as crystal, you would suppose the stream to be running sideways.

children.text: saṃsarpantyā sapadi bhavataḥ srotasi chāyayāsau syād asthānopagatayamunāsaṃgamevābhirāmā ||
children.translated_text: As your shadow at once creeps along her stream, she will be lovely, as though she had come to an improper confluence with the <s>Yamunā</s>.

children.text: āsīnānāṃ surabhitaśilaṃ nābhigandhair mṛgāṇāṃ tasyā eva prabhavam acalaṃ prāpya gauraṃ tuṣāraiḥ
children.translated_text: Having reached the pale mountain, made white by snow, the very source of that river, whose stones are fragrant with the navel-scent of deer sitting there,

children.text: vakṣyasy adhvaśramavinayena tasya śṛṅge niṣaṇṇaḥ śobhāṃ śubhrāṃ trinayanavṛṣotkhātapaṅkopameyam ||
children.translated_text: you will speak of its pure beauty, sitting on its peak to remove the fatigue of the road, a beauty comparable to the mud dug up by the bull of the three-eyed god.

children.text: taṃ ced vāyau sarati saralaskandhasaṃghaṭṭajanmā bādhetolkākṣapitacamarībālabhāro davāgniḥ
children.translated_text: If, while the wind moves, a forest fire born from the rubbing together of pine trunks should trouble that mountain, burning away the heavy tails of the <s>camarī</s> deer like firebrands,

children.text: arhasy enaṃ śamayitum alaṃ vāridhārāsahasrair āpannārtipraśamanaphalāḥ saṃpado hy uttamānām ||
children.translated_text: you ought to extinguish it with thousands of streams of water; for the riches of the noble have as their fruit the soothing of distress among the afflicted.

children.text: ye saṃrambhotpatanarabhasāḥ svāṅgabhaṅgāya tasmin muktādhvānaṃ sapadi śarabhā laṅghayeyur bhavantam
children.translated_text: If on that mountain the <s>śarabhas</s>, impetuous in their enraged leaps, should at once try to overleap you, who have left the path, only to break their own bodies,

children.text: tān kurvīthās tumulakarakāvṛṣṭipātāvakīrṇān ke vā na syuḥ paribhavapadaṃ niṣphalārambhayatnāḥ ||
children.translated_text: you should cover them with the fall of a tumultuous shower of hailstones; who indeed would not become an object of contempt when their undertaking is begun in vain?

children.text: tatra vyaktaṃ dṛṣadi caraṇanyāsam ardhendumauleḥ śaśvat siddhair upacitabaliṃ bhaktinamraḥ parīyāḥ
children.translated_text: There, where the footprint of the crescent-crested god is clearly visible on the rock, constantly honored with offerings by the <s>siddhas</s>, you should walk around it, bowed with devotion.

children.text: yasmin dṛṣṭe karaṇavigamād ūrdhvam uddhūtapāpāḥ kalpiṣyante sthiragaṇapadaprāptaye śraddadhānāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When that has been seen, believers, their sins shaken off after the departure of the senses, will be prepared for attaining a firm place among his attendants.

children.text: śabdāyante madhuram anilaiḥ kīcakāḥ pūryamāṇāḥ saṃraktābhis tripuravijayo gīyate kiṃnarībhiḥ
children.translated_text: The hollow reeds, filled by the winds, sound sweetly; the victory over <s>Tripura</s> is sung by flushed <s>kiṃnarī</s> women.

children.text: nirhrādas te muraja iva cet kandareṣu dhvaniḥ syāt saṃgītārtho nanu paśupates tatra bhāvī samagraḥ ||
children.translated_text: If your resonance in the caves should be like the sound of a drum, then surely the whole musical accompaniment for <s>Paśupati</s> will be complete there.

children.text: prāleyādrer upataṭam atikramya tāṃs tān viśeṣān haṃsadvāraṃ bhṛgupatiyaśovartma yat krauñcarandhram
children.translated_text: After passing the lower slope of the snowy mountain and its various wonders, follow the northern direction by the <s>Haṃsadvāra</s>, the hole of <s>Krauñca</s>, the path of <s>Bhṛgupati</s>'s fame.

children.text: tenodīcīṃ diśam anusares tiryag āyāmaśobhī śyāmaḥ pādo baliniyamanābhyudyatasyeva viṣṇoḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, dark and beautiful in your length stretched crosswise, you will be like the foot of <s>Viṣṇu</s> raised to restrain <s>Bali</s>.

children.text: gatvā cordhvaṃ daśamukhabhujocchvāsitaprasthasaṃdheḥ kailāsasya tridaśavanitādarpaṇasyātithiḥ syāḥ
children.translated_text: Then, having gone upward, become a guest of <s>Kailāsa</s>, whose tablelands' joints were loosened by the arms of the ten-headed one, and which is the mirror of the women of the gods.

children.text: śṛṅgocchrāyaiḥ kumudaviśadair yo vitatya sthitaḥ khaṃ rāśībhūtaḥ pratidinam iva tryambakasyāṭṭahāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With its lofty peaks, clear as white lotuses, it stands spreading through the sky, like the gathered laughter of <s>Tryambaka</s> every day.

children.text: utpaśyāmi tvayi taṭagate snigdhabhinnāñjanābhe sadyaḥ kṛttadviradadaśanacchedagaurasya tasya
children.translated_text: When you have reached its slope, your form resembling smooth split collyrium, I imagine that mountain, white like the freshly cut tusk-fragments of an elephant,

children.text: śobhām adreḥ stimitanayanaprekṣaṇīyāṃ bhavitrīm aṃsanyaste sati halabhṛto mecake vāsasīva ||
children.translated_text: will have a beauty worth gazing at with motionless eyes, as when a dark garment is laid upon the shoulder of <s>Halabhṛt</s>.

children.text: hitvā tasmin bhujagavalayaṃ śambhunā dattahastā krīḍāśaile yadi ca vicaret pādacāreṇa gaurī
children.translated_text: And if <s>Gaurī</s>, her serpent-bracelet set aside and her hand held by <s>Śambhu</s>, should wander on foot on that pleasure mountain,

children.text: bhaṅgībhaktyā viracitavapuḥ stambhitāntarjalaughaḥ sopānatvaṃ kuru maṇitaṭārohaṇāyāgrayāyī ||
children.translated_text: then, shaping your body with a succession of bends, with the mass of water within you held still, go ahead and become a staircase for her ascent to the jeweled slopes.

children.text: tatrāvaśyaṃ valayakuliśodghaṭṭanodgīrṇatoyaṃ neṣyanti tvāṃ surayuvatayo yantradhārāgṛhatvam
children.translated_text: There the young women of the gods will surely lead you into service as a fountain-house, with your water poured forth by the striking of their bracelet-thunderbolts.

children.text: tābhyo mokṣas tava yadi sakhe gharmalabdhasya na syāt krīḍālolāḥ śravaṇaparuṣair garjitair bhāyayes tāḥ ||
children.translated_text: If, my friend, you find no release from them once the heat has been obtained from you, then frighten those playful ones with thunderclaps harsh to the ear.

children.text: hemāmbhojaprasavi salilaṃ mānasasyādadānaḥ kurvan kāmaṃ kṣaṇamukhapaṭaprītim airāvatasya
children.translated_text: Taking up the water of <s>Mānasa</s>, which produces golden lotuses, and at will giving <s>Airāvata</s> the pleasure of a face-cloth for a moment,

children.text: dhunvan kalpadrumakisalayāny aṃśukānīva vātair nānāceṣṭair jaladalalitair nirviśes taṃ nagendram ||
children.translated_text: and shaking the tender shoots of the wish-fulfilling trees with winds like garments, enjoy that lord of mountains with various graceful cloud-actions.

children.text: tasyotsaṅge praṇayina iva srastagaṅgādukūlāṃ na tvaṃ dṛṣṭvā na punar alakāṃ jñāsyase kāmacārin
children.translated_text: On its lap, like that of a lover, with the <s>Gaṅgā</s> slipped down like a silk garment, when you see <s>Alakā</s>, wanderer at will, you will not fail to recognize her again.

children.text: yā vaḥ kāle vahati salilodgāram uccair vimānā muktājālagrathitam alakaṃ kāminīvābhravṛndam ||
children.translated_text: In season she bears lofty palaces pouring forth water, and clouds as locks of hair threaded with nets of pearls, like a woman.

children.text: Chapter 2
vidhunvantaṃ lalitavanitāḥ sendracāpaṃ sacitrāḥ saṃgītāya prahatamurajāḥ snigdhagambhīraghoṣam
children.translated_text: There, with graceful women shaking them, the palaces are variegated by rainbows; with drums struck for music, they have a smooth, deep sound.

children.text: antastoyaṃ maṇimayabhuvas tuṅgam abhraṃlihāgrāḥ prāsādās tvāṃ tulayitum alaṃ yatra tais tair viśeṣaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Containing water within, with jeweled floors and high cloud-touching summits, they are able to equal you by these and other special qualities.

children.text: haste līlākamalam alake bālakundānuviddhaṃ nītā lodhraprasavarajasā pāṇḍutām ānane śrīḥ
children.translated_text: There the women have a play-lotus in the hand, young jasmine woven into their locks, the beauty of the face made pale by the pollen of lodhra flowers,

children.text: cūḍāpāśe navakuravakaṃ cāru karṇe śirīṣaṃ sīmante ca tvadupagamajaṃ yatra nīpaṃ vadhūnām ||
children.translated_text: fresh <s>kuravaka</s> charming in the knot of hair, <s>śirīṣa</s> at the ear, and, in the parting of the hair, a <s>nīpa</s> flower born from your arrival.

children.text: yatronmattabhramaramukharāḥ pādapā nityapuṣpā haṃsaśreṇīracitaraśanā nityapadmā nalinyaḥ
children.translated_text: There the trees, noisy with intoxicated bees, are always in flower; the lotus ponds, whose girdles are formed by rows of swans, always have lotuses.

children.text: kekotkaṇṭhā bhuvanaśikhino nityabhāsvatkalāpā nityajyotsnāḥ prahitatamovṛttiramyāḥ pradoṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The domestic peacocks, longing for cries, always have shining tail-feathers; the twilights, always moonlit and with darkness dispelled, are lovely.

children.text: ānandotthaṃ nayanasalilaṃ yatra nānyair nimittair nānyas tāpaṃ kusumaśarajād iṣṭasaṃyogasādhyāt
children.translated_text: There tears in the eyes arise only from joy and from no other causes; there is no other heat than that born from the flower-arrowed god and curable by union with the beloved.

children.text: nāpy anyasmāt praṇayakalahād viprayogopapattir vitteśānāṃ na ca khalu vayo yauvanād anyad asti ||
children.translated_text: Nor is there occasion for separation from anything except a lovers' quarrel; and for the attendants of the lord of wealth there is indeed no age other than youth.

children.text: yasyāṃ yakṣāḥ sitamaṇimayāny etya harmyasthalāni jyotiśchāyākusumaracitāny uttamastrīsahāyāḥ
children.translated_text: In that city the <s>yakṣas</s>, going to palace terraces made of white crystal, with excellent women as companions, where flowers are fashioned from light and shadow,

children.text: āsevante madhu ratiphalaṃ kalpavṛkṣaprasūtaṃ tvadgambhīradhvaniṣu śanakaiḥ puṣkareṣv āhateṣu ||
children.translated_text: enjoy wine, the fruit of love, produced by wish-fulfilling trees, while your deep sounds gently strike upon the drumheads.

children.text: mandākinyāḥ salilaśiśiraiḥ sevyamānā marudbhir mandārāṇām anutaṭaruhāṃ chāyayā vāritoṣṇāḥ
children.translated_text: Cooled by breezes chilled with the water of the <s>Mandākinī</s>, and protected from heat by the shade of <s>mandāra</s> trees growing along its banks,

children.text: anveṣṭavyaiḥ kanakasikatāmuṣṭinikṣepagūḍhaiḥ saṃkrīḍante maṇibhiramaraprārthitayā yatra kanyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There the maidens play with jewels sought even by the immortals, hidden by throwing down handfuls of golden sand which must then be searched for.

children.text: nīvībandhocchvāsitaśithilaṃ yatra bimbādharāṇāṃ kṣaumaṃ rāgādanibhṛtakareṣv ākṣipatsu priyeṣu
children.translated_text: There, when their beloveds, with hands restless from passion, tug at the linen garments of women with bimba-red lips, loosened and slack from the heaving of the knot at the waist,

children.text: arcistuṅgān abhimukham api prāpya ratnapradīpān hrīmūḍhānāṃ bhavati viphalapreraṇā cūrṇamuṣṭiḥ ||
children.translated_text: even when they face the jewel-lamps with their high flames, the handful of powder thrown by the bashful and bewildered women to put them out is useless.

children.text: netrā nītāḥ satatagatinā yadvimānāgrabhūmīr ālekhyānāṃ salilakaṇikādoṣam utpādya sadyaḥ
children.translated_text: There winds, driven by constant motion to the upper terraces of the mansions, at once create the fault of water-drops on the paintings;

children.text: śaṅkāspṛṣṭā iva jalamucas tvādṛśā jālamārgair dhūmodgārānukṛtinipuṇā jarjarā niṣpatanti ||
children.translated_text: then, as if touched by fear of clouds like you, they slip out through the lattice-windows, worn thin, skilled in imitating outbursts of smoke.

children.text: yatra strīṇāṃ priyatamabhujocchvāsitāliṅgitānām aṅgaglāniṃ suratajanitāṃ tantujālāvalambāḥ
children.translated_text: There, at midnight, moonstones, hanging from nets of threads, with clear moonbeams after your obstruction has passed away,

children.text: tvatsaṃrodhāpagamaviśadaiś candrapādair niśīthe vyālumpanti sphuṭajalalavasyandinaś candrakāntāḥ ||
children.translated_text: wipe away the bodily languor born of lovemaking from women clasped so that their lovers' arms have left them breathless, while the stones drip distinct drops of water.

children.text: akṣayyāntarbhavananidhayaḥ pratyahaṃ raktakaṇṭhair udgāyadbhir dhanapatiyaśaḥ kiṃnarair yatra sārdham
children.translated_text: There lovers, together with <s>kinnaras</s> whose throats are ever reddened as they sing each day the glory of the lord of wealth,

children.text: vaibhrājākhyaṃ vibudhavanitāvāramukhyāsahāyā baddhālāpā bahirupavanaṃ kāmino nirviśanti ||
children.translated_text: enjoy the outer pleasure-grove called <s>Vaibhrāja</s>, accompanied by chief courtesans among the women of the gods and engaged in conversation with them.

children.text: gatyutkampād alakapatitair yatra mandārapuṣpaiḥ putracchedaiḥ kanakakamalaiḥ karṇavisraṃsibhiś ca
children.translated_text: There the night-path of amorous women is indicated at sunrise by mandara flowers fallen from their hair through the shaking of their gait, by cut shoots, by golden lotuses slipped from their ears,

children.text: muktājālaiḥ stanaparisaracchinnasūtraiś ca hārair naiśo mārgaḥ savitur udaye sūcyate kāminīnām ||
children.translated_text: and by pearl nets and necklaces whose threads have snapped near their breasts.

children.text: vāsaś citraṃ madhu nayanayor vibhramādeśadakṣaṃ puṣpodbhedaṃ saha kisalayair bhūṣaṇānāṃ vikalpam
children.translated_text: In that city a single wish-fulfilling tree produces everything that adorns women: bright garments, wine, the skill that instructs the eyes in amorous play, flowers together with young shoots, varieties of ornaments,

children.text: lākṣārāgaṃ caraṇakamalanyāsayogyaṃ ca yasyām ekaḥ sūte sakalam abalāmaṇḍanaṃ kalpavṛkṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and lac-dye fit for setting upon their lotus-like feet.

children.text: patraśyāmā dinakarahayaspardhino yatra vāhāḥ śailodagrās tvam iva kariṇo vṛṣṭimantaḥ prabhedāt
children.translated_text: There the horses are dark as leaves and rival the steeds of the sun; the elephants, like you, are lofty as mountains and pour with rut-fluid from their temples;

children.text: yodhāgraṇyaḥ pratidaśamukhaṃ saṃyuge tasthivāṃsaḥ pratyādiṣṭābharaṇarucayaś candrahāsavraṇāṅkaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the foremost warriors, who stood in battle against ten-headed <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, have their ornaments' beauty surpassed by scars from <s>Candrahāsa</s>.

children.text: matvā devaṃ dhanapatisakhaṃ yatra sākṣād vasantaṃ prāyaś cāpaṃ na vahati bhayān manmathaḥ ṣaṭpadajyam
children.translated_text: There, thinking the god, friend of the lord of wealth, to be spring itself in visible form, <s>Manmatha</s> generally does not carry his bow with its bee-string out of fear;

children.text: sabhrūbhaṅgaprahitanayanaiḥ kāmilakṣyeṣv amoghais tasyārambhaś caturavanitāvibhramair eva siddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: his undertaking against the targets of lovers is accomplished by the very coquetries of clever women, whose glances are sent forth with knitted brows and never miss.

children.text: tatrāgāraṃ dhanapatigṛhān uttareṇāsmadīyaṃ dūrāl lakṣyaṃ surapatidhanuścāruṇā toraṇena
children.translated_text: There, north of the lord of wealth's palace, is my house, visible from afar by its gateway beautiful with the rainbow of <s>Indra</s>;

children.text: yasyopānte kṛtakatanayaḥ kāntayā vardhito me hastaprāpyastabakanamito bālamandāravṛkṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: beside it stands a young mandara tree, bent down by clusters within hand's reach, treated by my beloved as an adopted child and nurtured by her.

children.text: vāpī cāsmin marakataśilābaddhasopānamārgā haimaiśchannā vikacakamalaiḥ snigdhavaidūryanālaiḥ
children.translated_text: In it there is also a step-well whose stairway is built of emerald slabs, covered with golden lotuses in full bloom and with glossy vaidūrya stems;

children.text: yasyās toye kṛtavasatayo mānasaṃ saṃnikṛṣṭaṃ nādhyāsyanti vyapagataśucas tvām api prekṣya haṃsāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the swans who have made their homes in its water, with <s>Mānasa</s> close by, will not long for that lake once their sorrow has passed away, even when they see you.

children.text: tasyās tīre racitaśikharaḥ peśalair indranīlaiḥ krīḍāśailaḥ kanakakadalīveṣṭanaprekṣaṇīyaḥ
children.translated_text: On its bank is a pleasure-hill with a peak fashioned of smooth sapphires, beautiful to behold with its encircling golden plantains;

children.text: madgehinyāḥ priya iti sakhe cetasā kātareṇa prekṣyopāntasphuritataḍitaṃ tvāṃ tam eva smarāmi ||
children.translated_text: because it is dear to my wife, friend, when I see you with lightning quivering at your edge, my anxious heart remembers that very hill.

children.text: raktāśokaś calakisalayaḥ kesaraś cātra kāntaḥ pratyāsannau kuruvakavṛter mādhavīmaṇḍapasya
children.translated_text: Here too, near the arbor of mādhavī creeper enclosed by a hedge of kuruvaka, stand a red aśoka with trembling young leaves and a lovely bakula tree;

children.text: ekaḥ sakhyās tava saha mayā vāmapādābhilāṣī kāṅkṣaty anyo vadanamadirāṃ dohadacchadmanāsyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: one of them longs, along with me, for the left foot of your friend, while the other, under the pretext of its blossom-rite, desires the wine of her mouth.

children.text: tanmadhye ca sphaṭikaphalakā kāñcanī vāsayaṣṭir mūle baddhā maṇibhir anatiprauḍhavaṃśaprakāśaiḥ
children.translated_text: Between them is a golden perch with a crystal slab, set at its base with jewels that shine like not yet fully grown bamboo shoots;

children.text: tālaiḥ śiñjāvalayasubhagair nartitaḥ kāntayā me yām adhyāste divasavigame nīlakaṇṭhaḥ suhṛd vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: at day’s end a peacock, your friend, sits upon it, made to dance by my beloved to rhythms made lovely by her jingling bracelets.

children.text: ebhiḥ sādho hṛdayanihitair lakṣaṇair lakṣayethā dvāropānte likhitavapuṣau śaṅkhapadmau ca dṛṣṭvā
children.translated_text: Good one, by these signs kept in your heart you should recognize it, and also by seeing near the doorway figures of a conch and lotus drawn there.

children.text: kṣāmacchāyaṃ bhavanam adhunā madviyogena nūnaṃ sūryāpāye na khalu kamalaṃ puṣyati svāmabhikhyām ||
children.translated_text: Because of my separation, the house is now surely pale and dim; for when the sun is gone, the lotus does not preserve its own beauty.

children.text: gatvā sadyaḥ kalabhatanutāṃ śīghrasaṃpātahetoḥ krīḍāśaile prathamakathite ramyasānau niṣaṇṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Having at once become as small-bodied as a young elephant for the sake of a swift descent, and seated on the lovely slope of the pleasure-hill described first,

children.text: arhasy antarbhavanapatitāṃ kartum alpālpabhāsaṃ khadyotālīvilasitanibhāṃ vidyudunmeṣadṛṣṭim ||
children.translated_text: you should direct into the inner apartments a lightning-flash glance, faintly gleaming, like the play of a row of fireflies.

children.text: tanvī śyāmā śikharidaśanā pakvabimbādharauṣṭhī madhye kṣāmā cakitahariṇīprekṣaṇā nimnanābhiḥ
children.translated_text: She who is slender, dark, with peaked teeth and lips like ripe bimba fruit, thin at the waist, with the startled glance of a doe and a deep navel,

children.text: śroṇībhārād alasagamanā stokanamrā stanābhyāṃ yā tatra syād yuvatīviṣaye sṛṣṭir ādyaiva dhātuḥ ||
children.translated_text: slow in gait from the weight of her hips and slightly bent by her breasts, would be there, the Creator's very first creation in the matter of young women.

children.text: tāṃ jānīthāḥ parimitakathāṃ jīvitaṃ me dvitīyaṃ dūrībhūte mayi sahacare cakravākīm ivaikām
children.translated_text: Know her, sparing in speech, to be my second life, alone like a cakravākī when I, her companion, am far away;

children.text: gāḍhotkaṇṭhāṃ guruṣu divaseṣv eṣu gacchatsu bālāṃ jātāṃ manye śiśiramathitāṃ padminīṃ vānyarūpām ||
children.translated_text: as these heavy days pass, I think the young woman, deeply yearning, has become changed in form, like a lotus plant battered by frost.

children.text: nūnaṃ tasyāḥ prabalaruditocchūnanetraṃ priyāyā niḥśvāsānām aśiśiratayā bhinnavarṇādharoṣṭham
children.translated_text: Surely the face of my beloved, her eyes swollen from violent weeping, her lower lip discolored by the heat of her sighs,

children.text: hastanyastaṃ mukham asakalavyakti lambālakatvād indor dainyaṃ tvadanusaraṇakliṣṭakānter bibharti ||
children.translated_text: resting upon her hand and only partly visible because of her long locks, bears the pitiable state of the moon whose splendor is wearied by following you.

children.text: āloke te nipatati purā sā balivyākulā vā matsādṛśyaṃ virahatanu vā bhāvagamyaṃ likhantī
children.translated_text: Before your eyes fall on her, she may be troubled with offerings, or she may be drawing my likeness, thinned by separation and perceptible only through feeling;

children.text: pṛcchantī vā madhuravacanāṃ sārikāṃ pañjarasthāṃ kaccid bhartuḥ smarasi rasike tvaṃ hi tasya priyeti ||
children.translated_text: or she may be asking the sweet-speaking <s>sārikā</s> bird confined in its cage, 'My clever one, do you remember your master? For you were dear to him.'

children.text: utsaṅge vā malinavasane saumya nikṣipya vīṇāṃ madgotrāṅkaṃ viracitapadaṃ geyam udgātukāmā
children.translated_text: Or, gentle one, laying a vīṇā in her lap upon her soiled garment, wishing to sing a song whose words were composed and marked with my family-name,

children.text: tantrīm ārdrāṃ nayanasalilaiḥ sārayitvā kathaṃcid bhūyo bhūyaḥ svayam api kṛtāṃ mūrcchanāṃ vismarantī ||
children.translated_text: after somehow setting right a string wet with the water of her eyes, she may again and again forget the melody which she herself had made.

children.text: śeṣān māsān virahadivasasthāpitasyāvadher vā vinyasyantī bhuvi gaṇanayā dehalīdattapuṣpaiḥ
children.translated_text: Or she may be arranging on the ground, for counting, flowers placed on the threshold to mark the remaining months of the limit fixed for the days of separation;

children.text: sambhogaṃ vā hṛdayanihitārambham āsvādayantī prāyeṇaite ramaṇaviraheṣv aṅganānāṃ vinodāḥ ||
children.translated_text: or she may be savoring a union begun and held in her heart. Such, for the most part, are the diversions of women in separation from their lovers.

children.text: savyāpārām ahani na tathā pīḍayed viprayogaḥ śaṅke rātrau gurutaraśucaṃ nirvinodāṃ sakhīṃ te
children.translated_text: Separation will not torment her so much in the daytime, when she has occupations; but at night, I fear, your friend, without diversion, will have far heavier grief.

children.text: matsaṃdeśaiḥ sukhayitum alaṃ paśya sādhvīṃ niśīthe tām unnidrām avaniśayanāṃ saudhavātāyanasthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At midnight, standing at the palace window, look upon that faithful woman, sleepless and lying on the ground, so that you may be able to comfort her with my messages.

children.text: ādhikṣāmāṃ virahaśayane saṃniṣaṇṇaikapārśvāṃ prācīmūle tanum iva kalāmātraśeṣāṃ himāṃśoḥ
children.translated_text: Emaciated by sorrow, lying on one side on the bed of separation, like the eastern crescent of the moon reduced to a mere slender digit,

children.text: nītā rātriḥ kṣaṇa iva mayā sārdham icchāratair yā tām evoṣṇair virahamahatīm aśrubhir yāpayantīm ||
children.translated_text: she is passing with hot tears that very night, made long by separation, which, when spent with me in desired pleasures, passed like a moment.

children.text: pādān indor amṛtaśiśirāñjalamārgapraviṣṭān pūrvaprītyā gatam abhimukhaṃ saṃnivṛttaṃ tathaiva
children.translated_text: Her eye, from old affection, has turned toward the moonbeams, cool as nectar, that have entered through the lattice path, and then has turned back in the same way;

children.text: cakṣuḥ khedāt salilagurubhiḥ pakṣmabhiśchādayantīṃ sābhre 'hnīva sthalakamalinī na prabuddhāṃ na suptām ||
children.translated_text: from weariness she covers it with lashes heavy with tears, like a land-lotus on a cloudy day, neither awake nor asleep.

children.text: niḥśvāsenādharakisalayakleśinā vikṣipantīṃ śuddhasnānāt paruṣamalakaṃ nūnam āgaṇḍalambam
children.translated_text: With a sigh that hurts her sprout-like lower lip, she surely tosses aside the rough curl, rough from pure bathing, hanging down to her cheek;

children.text: matsaṃbhogaḥ kathamupanamet svapnajo 'pīti nidrām ākāṅkṣantīṃ nayanasalilotpīḍaruddhāvakāśam ||
children.translated_text: she longs for sleep, thinking, 'Might union with him come to me even in a dream?' but its space is blocked by the flood of tears from her eyes.

children.text: ādye baddhā virahadivase yā śikhā dāma hitvā śāpasyānte vigalitaśucā tāṃ mayodveṣṭanīyām
children.translated_text: The braid which, on the first day of separation, she bound after casting off her garland, and which I must unbind when the curse ends and her sorrow has melted away,

children.text: sparśakliṣṭām ayamitanakhenāsakṛtsārayantīṃ gaṇḍābhogāt kaṭhinaviṣamām ekaveṇīṃ kareṇa ||
children.translated_text: that single braid, painful to touch, hard and uneven from lying on her cheek, she keeps moving again and again with her hand and untrimmed nails.

children.text: sā saṃnyastābharaṇam abalā peśalaṃ dhārayantī śayyotsaṅge nihitam asakṛd duḥkhaduḥkhena gātram
children.translated_text: That helpless woman, having laid aside her ornaments and bearing her delicate body on the edge of the bed, again and again, with one grief upon another,

children.text: tvām apy asraṃ navajalamayaṃ mocayiṣyaty avaśyaṃ prāyaḥ sarvo bhavati karuṇāvṛttir ārdrāntarātmā ||
children.translated_text: will certainly make you too shed tears made of fresh water; for nearly everyone whose inner self is tender becomes moved by compassion.

children.text: jāne sakhyās tava mayi manaḥ saṃbhṛtasnehamasmād itthaṃbhūtāṃ prathamavirahe tām ahaṃ tarkayāmi
children.translated_text: From this I know that your friend's mind is full of affection for me; such is how I imagine her in this first separation.

children.text: vācālaṃ māṃ na khalu subhagaṃmanyabhāvaḥ karoti pratyakṣaṃ te nikhilam acirād bhrātar uktaṃ mayā yat ||
children.translated_text: No conceit of thinking myself fortunate makes me talkative. Soon, brother, everything that I have said will be directly before your eyes.

children.text: ruddhāpāṅgaprasaram alakair añjanasnehaśūnyaṃ pratyādeśād api ca madhuno vismṛtabhrūvilāsam
children.translated_text: Her eye, its sideward glance obstructed by curls and lacking the smoothness of collyrium, and, because wine has been renounced, having forgotten the play of the eyebrow,

children.text: tvayy āsanne nayanam uparispandi śaṅke mṛgākṣyā mīnakṣobhāc calakuvalayaśrītulām eṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: when you are near, will, I think, quiver above and attain a likeness to the beauty of a moving blue lotus stirred by a fish.

children.text: vāmaś cāsyāḥ kararuhapadair mucyamāno madīyair muktājālaṃ ciraparicitaṃ tyājito daivagatyā
children.translated_text: And her left thigh, released from the nail-marks made by me, deprived by fate of its long-familiar net of pearls,

children.text: saṃbhogānte mama samucito hastasaṃvāhamānāṃ yāsyaty ūruḥ sarasakadalīstambhagauraś calatvam ||
children.translated_text: pale like the juicy trunk of a plantain and accustomed, after love-making, to the touch of my hand, will begin to tremble.

children.text: tasmin kāle jalada yadi sā labdhanidrāsukhā syād anvāsyaināṃ stanitavimukho yāmamātraṃ sahasva
children.translated_text: At that time, cloud, if she has obtained the pleasure of sleep, sit beside her and, turning away from thunder, endure it for the space of a watch.

children.text: mā bhūd asyāḥ praṇayini mayi svapnalabdhe kathaṃcit sadyaḥ kaṇṭhacyutabhujalatāgranthi gāḍhopagūḍham ||
children.translated_text: Let it not happen that, when she has somehow obtained me, her lover, in a dream, the tight embrace of her vine-like arms should suddenly slip from my neck.

children.text: tām utthāpya svajalakaṇikāśītalenānilena pratyāśvastāṃ samam abhinavair jālakair mālatīnām
children.translated_text: Having awakened her with a breeze cooled by your own drops of water, and reassured her together with the fresh buds of the jasmine vines,

children.text: vidyudgarbhaḥ stimitanayanāṃ tvatsanāthe gavākṣe vaktuṃ dhīraḥ stanitavacanair māninīṃ prakramethāḥ ||
children.translated_text: with lightning within you, while her eyes are still motionless, you should begin, in steady words of thunder, to speak to that proud woman at the window where you are her protector.

children.text: bhartur mitraṃ priyam avidhave viddhi mām ambuvāhaṃ tatsaṃdeśair hṛdayanihitair āgataṃ tvatsamīpam
children.translated_text: 'O woman whose husband lives, know me, the rain-bearer, to be your husband's dear friend, come near you with his messages held in my heart.

children.text: yo vṛndāni tvarayati pathi śrāmyatāṃ proṣitānāṃ mandrasnigdhair dhvanibhir abalāveṇimokṣotsukāni ||
children.translated_text: On the road I hasten the groups of weary men living abroad, by my deep, gentle sounds, making their wives eager to unbind their braids.'

children.text: ity ākhyāte pavanatanayaṃ maithilīvonmukhī sā tvām utkaṇṭhocchvasitahṛdayā vīkṣya saṃbhāvya caiva
children.translated_text: When this has been said, like <s>Maithilī</s> toward the son of the Wind, she will look up at you, seeing and respectfully receiving you, her heart sighing with longing.

children.text: śroṣyaty asmāt param avahitā saumya sīmantinīnāṃ kāntodantaḥ suhṛdupanataḥ saṃgamāt kiṃcid ūnaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, gentle one, she will listen attentively to what follows; for news of a husband, brought by a friend, is only a little less than union for married women.

children.text: tām āyuṣman mama ca vacanād ātmanaś copakartuṃ brūyā evaṃ tava sahacaro rāmagiryāśramasthaḥ
children.translated_text: To her, long-lived one, for my sake and in order to benefit yourself as well, you should say this: 'Your companion, dwelling in the hermitage on <s>Rāmagiri</s>,

children.text: avyāpannaḥ kuśalam abale pṛcchati tvāṃ viyuktaḥ pūrvābhāṣyaṃ sulabhavipadāṃ prāṇinām etad eva ||
children.translated_text: unharmed and separated from you, asks after your welfare, helpless one. This is the first thing to be said among living beings whose misfortunes come easily.'

children.text: aṅgenāṅgaṃ pratanu tanunā gāḍhataptena taptaṃ sāsreṇāśrudrutam aviratotkaṇṭham utkaṇṭhitena
children.translated_text: Far away, he enters, by those imaginings, limb into limb, his slender body into your slender body, his intensely heated body into yours, heated by pain, his tearful body into yours dissolved by tears, his ceaselessly longing body into yours that longs,

children.text: uṣṇocchvāsaṃ samadhikatarocchvāsinā dūravartī saṃkalpais tair viśati vidhinā vairiṇā ruddhamārgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: his hot sigh into yours that sighs still more deeply; but by hostile fate his path is blocked.

children.text: śabdākhyeyaṃ yadapi kila te yaḥ sakhīnāṃ purastāt karṇe lolaḥ kathayitum abhūd ānanasparśalobhāt
children.translated_text: Though that message, which must be called speech, was something I had once been eager to tell you in your ear before your friends, restless from desire to touch your face,

children.text: so 'tikrāntaḥ śravaṇaviṣayaṃ locanābhyām adṛṣṭas tvām utkaṇṭhāviracitapadaṃ manmukhenedam āha ||
children.translated_text: it has passed beyond the range of hearing and is unseen by the eyes; now, with its words shaped by longing for you, it says this through my mouth.

children.text: śyāmāsv aṅgaṃ cakitahariṇīprekṣaṇe dṛṣṭipātaṃ vaktracchāyāṃ śaśini śikhināṃ barhabhāreṣu keśān
children.translated_text: In dark creepers I see your body, in the startled doe's glance the fall of your eyes, in the moon the shadow of your face, in the masses of peacock plumes your hair,

children.text: utpaśyāmi pratanuṣu nadīvīciṣu bhrūvilāsān hantaikasmin kvacid api na te caṇḍi sādṛśyam asti ||
children.translated_text: and in the slender waves of rivers the play of your eyebrows; alas, fierce one, nowhere in any single thing is there a likeness of you.

children.text: tvām ālikhya praṇayakupitāṃ dhāturāgaiḥ śilāyām ātmānaṃ te caraṇapatitaṃ yāvad icchāmi kartum
children.translated_text: After drawing you on a rock with mineral colors, angry in love, when I wish to make myself fallen at your feet,

children.text: asrais tāvan muhur upacitair dṛṣṭir ālupyate me krūras tasminn api na sahate saṃgamaṃ nau kṛtāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: my sight is at once blurred by tears that repeatedly gather; cruel fate does not allow even there a union of us two.

children.text: dhārāsiktasthalasurabhiṇas tvanmukhasyāsya bāle dūrībhūtaṃ pratanum api māṃ pañcabāṇaḥ kṣiṇoti
children.translated_text: O young girl, <s>Pañcabāṇa</s>, the five-arrowed Love, wastes even me, thin and far away from this face of yours, whose ground is fragrant when sprinkled by showers.

children.text: gharmānte 'smin vigaṇaya kathaṃ vāsarāṇi vrajeyur diksaṃsaktapravitataghanavyastasūryātapāni ||
children.translated_text: Consider how, in this end of summer, the days could pass, when the sun's heat is scattered by widespread clouds clinging to the quarters.

children.text: mām ākāśapraṇihitabhujaṃ nirdayāśleṣahetor labdhāyās te kathamapi mayā svapnasaṃdarśaneṣu
children.translated_text: When somehow I have obtained a sight of you in dreams, and stretch my arms into empty space for the sake of a pitiless embrace,

children.text: paśyantīnāṃ na khalu bahuśo na sthalīdevatānāṃ muktāsthūlās tarukisalayeṣv aśruleśāḥ patanti ||
children.translated_text: the large pearl-like drops of tears do indeed often fall upon the tree-shoots from the eyes of the local goddesses who watch me.

children.text: bhittvā sadyaḥ kisalayapuṭān devadārudrumāṇāṃ ye tatkṣīrasrutisurabhayo dakṣiṇena pravṛttāḥ
children.translated_text: Those southern winds which have arisen after immediately splitting the leaf-buds of the deodar trees, fragrant with the flowing of their sap,

children.text: āliṅgyante guṇavati mayā te tuṣārādrivātāḥ pūrvaṃ spṛṣṭaṃ yadi kila bhaved aṅgam ebhis taveti ||
children.translated_text: I embrace, O virtuous one, thinking, 'Perhaps your body may first have been touched by these.'

children.text: saṃkṣipyante kṣaṇa iva kathaṃ dīrghayāmā triyāmā sarvāvasthāsv ahar api kathaṃ mandamandātapaṃ syāt
children.translated_text: How might the night, with its long watches, be shortened as if to a moment? How might the day too, in all states, have very gentle heat?

children.text: itthaṃ cetaś caṭulanayane durlabhaprārthanaṃ me gāḍhoṣmābhiḥ kṛtam aśaraṇaṃ tvadviyogavyathābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, O restless-eyed one, my mind, made helpless by the burning pains of separation from you, forms wishes that are hard to obtain.

children.text: nanv ātmānaṃ bahu vigaṇayann ātmanaivāvalambe tatkalyāṇi tvam api nitarāṃ mā gamaḥ kātaratvam
children.translated_text: Surely, counting myself much, I support myself by myself; therefore, O auspicious one, you too must not sink too deeply into timidity.

children.text: kasyātyantaṃ sukham upanataṃ duḥkham ekāntato vā nīcair gacchaty upari ca daśā cakranemikrameṇa ||
children.translated_text: To whom has happiness come absolutely, or sorrow entirely? A person's condition goes down and up in the manner of a wheel-rim.

children.text: śāpānto me bhujagaśayanād utthite śārṅgapāṇau śeṣān māsān gamaya caturo locane mīlayitvā
children.translated_text: My curse will end when <s>Śārṅgapāṇi</s> rises from the serpent couch; pass the remaining four months with your eyes closed.

children.text: paścād āvāṃ virahaguṇitaṃ taṃ tam ātmābhilāṣaṃ nirvekṣyāvaḥ pariṇataśaraccandrikāsu kṣapāsu ||
children.translated_text: Afterward the two of us, through nights bright with the fully ripened autumn moonlight, shall enjoy each desire of our hearts, increased by separation.

children.text: bhūyaścāha tvam api śayane kaṇṭhalagnā purā me nidrāṃ gatvā kimapi rudatī sasvaraṃ viprabuddhā
children.translated_text: And again he says: Once, while you were clinging to my neck on the bed, you fell asleep and, waking with a cry, wept for some reason.

children.text: sāntarhāsaṃ kathitam asakṛt pṛcchataś ca tvayā me dṛṣṭaḥ svapne kitava ramayan kāmapi tvaṃ mayeti ||
children.translated_text: When I repeatedly asked you, you told me with a hidden smile, 'O rogue, I saw in a dream that you were making love to some woman.'

children.text: etasmān māṃ kuśalinam abhijñānadānād viditvā mā kaulīnād asitanayane mayy aviśvāsinī bhūḥ
children.translated_text: Knowing from this token of recognition that I am well, O dark-eyed one, do not become distrustful of me because of gossip.

children.text: snehān āhuḥ kimapi virahe dhvaṃsinas te tv abhogād iṣṭe vastuny upacitarasāḥ premarāśībhavanti ||
children.translated_text: They say affections somehow decay in separation; but yours, from lack of enjoyment, become heaps of love with flavor increased toward the desired object.

children.text: āśvāsyaivaṃ prathamavirahodagraśokāṃ sakhīṃ te śailād āśu trinayanavṛṣotkhātakūṭān nivṛttaḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus consoled your friend, whose grief is intense in her first separation, quickly return from the mountain whose peaks were dug up by the bull of the three-eyed god.

children.text: sābhijñānaprahitakuśalais tadvacobhir mamāpi prātaḥ kundaprasavaśithilaṃ jīvitaṃ dhārayethāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And with those words of hers, sent with tokens of recognition and news of welfare, you should sustain my own life, which in the morning is loosened like a jasmine blossom.

children.text: kaccit saumya vyavasitam idaṃ bandhukṛtyaṃ tvayā me pratyādeśān na khalu bhavato dhīratāṃ kalpayāmi
children.translated_text: Gentle one, I hope this friendly service has been resolved upon by you. I do not infer your steadiness from any spoken reply,

children.text: niḥśabdo 'pi pradiśasi jalaṃ yācitaś cātakebhyaḥ pratyuktaṃ hi praṇayiṣu satām īpsitārthakriyaiva ||
children.translated_text: for even when silent you give water to the cātakas when asked; among the noble, the true answer to those who love them is simply the performance of the desired act.
